headline: New visitors convert at 43.9% from checkout to payment info, lower than the rest of the shop.
causes: Forced account creation or mandatory registration prompt at checkout. | Unexpected shipping fees revealed at the payment entry step.
checks: Run a conversion report comparing guest checkout users against account creation users during checkout. | Watch session recordings of new visitors dropping off between checkout and payment info to observe form friction.
experiments: Prominent Guest Checkout: If we display a prominent guest checkout option, then checkout → payment info conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time buyers avoid account creation friction.
caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

headline: New visitors convert at 22.3% from view item to add to cart, underperforming the rest of the shop.
causes: Lack of visible product reviews or trust badges on item pages. | Unclear sizing details, specifications, or stock availability.
checks: Check product page add-to-cart conversion rates segmented by new versus returning visitors. | Review mobile and desktop product detail pages to test page load speed and clarity of the add-to-cart button.
experiments: Product Page Trust Badges and Reviews: If we display star ratings and money-back guarantees near the add-to-cart button, then view item → add to cart conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time buyers gain trust in the product.
caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

headline: New visitors convert at 20.0% from visit to view item, lagging behind the rest of the shop.
causes: Generic homepage layout that fails to surface popular products. | Mismatch between acquisition landing pages and initial user expectations.
checks: Review landing page click-through rates to product pages for new visitors across top traffic channels. | Test homepage category navigation on mobile devices to evaluate visual clarity for first-time users.
experiments: Featured Product Category Grid: If we feature top-selling product categories directly on the main landing page, then visit → view item conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time visitors can quickly locate relevant items.
caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

headline: New visitors convert at 51.3% from add to cart to checkout, trailing the rest of the shop.
causes: Lack of shipping cost estimates or free shipping thresholds inside the cart. | Unclear or low-contrast checkout call-to-action button in the cart drawer.
checks: Analyze cart page abandonment reports specifically for first-time visitors. | Examine session recordings of cart views where new visitors do not click the checkout button.
experiments: Free Shipping Progress Bar in Cart: If we show a free shipping threshold progress bar in the cart, then add to cart → checkout conversion for new visitors will increase, because transparent savings incentives encourage starting checkout.
caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

headline: Organic first-touch visitors convert at 56.8% from checkout to payment info, lower than the shop average.
causes: Prominent promo code field prompting users to leave checkout. | Missing payment security badges for users discovering the store via search.
checks: Check checkout drop-off rates for organic search landing traffic. | Inspect session recordings of organic users at the checkout step to see if they highlight or copy text from discount code inputs.
experiments: Collapsed Promo Code Field: If we collapse the promo code input behind a text link during checkout, then checkout → payment info conversion for organic visitors will increase, because shoppers will not leave the checkout flow to look for coupons.
caveat: Channel indicates how the user first arrived at the shop, so attribution reflects intent differences inherent to organic search acquisition.

headline: Referral traffic converts at 46.6% from checkout to payment info, lower than the 60.0% rest of shop conversion.
causes: Mismatched expectations | Technical issues with referral parameters
checks: Identify the top referral sites and test the checkout flow specifically from those domains. | Check if referral traffic is experiencing any specific browser or device compatibility issues at the payment step.
experiments: Referral Landing Page Alignment: If we ensure the checkout experience matches the messaging from the referral source, then conversion will increase because users will feel a consistent journey.
